title: Fine-grained descending control of steering in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. 3D, Fig. 4A-C, Fig. S4D (left); Results 'Different descending neurons drive distinctive leg gestures'
quote: In experimental flies, we found that a brief pulse of light (200 ms) triggered a turn in the direction of the stimulated cell
mapping_basis: DNa02 is a MANC type name mapping to one type; hemidrivers R75C10AD/R87D07DBD are those of SS00730 (DNa02).
stimulation: 620/60 nm mercury-lamp light, 0.09 mW/mm2 over head and thorax, 200 ms pulses (2 s pulses also delivered)
type_coverage: one of the two DNa02 cells (unilateral, mosaic SPARC)
sensory_condition: tethered on spherical treadmill, norpA blind background, head capsule closed, wings removed

a few abdominal ganglion cells in some flies
coordination_notes: Ipsilateral stride length decreased in all three ipsilateral legs via a shortened return stroke; power stroke unaffected; contralateral legs unaffected; step direction of both front legs (and ipsilateral mid leg) shifted into the turn.
notes: Trials were included only if the fly kept forward velocity >= 1 mm/s around stimulation, so these are steering changes in already-walking flies; leg-rhythm fields not_assessed per PROTOCOL 3. Forward velocity unchanged (p = 0.802).
